who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), test-strength lint lane, worktree blaze-merge-1113
what: A lane that writes new code by copying the files around it (magic.rs, implicit_allocator.rs itself) copies their `// alloc: <why>` comments, but those comments stopped exempting anything on 2026-11-13. Now each one counts against the crate's row in alloc-sites.txt, and the implied allocations under them are still denied. This lane wrote 118 such comments and removed them with ast-grep (a line_comment rule with regex `^// alloc:`). It left the allocations themselves for `blaze check --fix`, because it may not run blaze.
cost: one ast-grep pass, plus a `blaze check --fix` and a fmt pass for the main agent; about 150 implied allocations to name
cause: the old idiom is still all over the crate that enforces the new one, so the nearest example teaches the banned form
class: a rule changed in one place while its examples elsewhere still show the old form, so new code copies what is now banned
prevention: run `blaze check --fix -p blaze-lints` over the whole crate once, so no `// alloc:` line is left to copy and the row in alloc-sites.txt goes to 0
workaround: write `Vec::new_in(Global)`, `Vec::with_capacity_in(n, Global)` and `blaze_mem::format_in!(Global, ..)` from the start, with `#![feature(allocator_api)]` already at crates/blaze-lints/src/lib.rs:10
